observation.visible_scene: A close, top-down view of a wet grey concrete/stone surface holding a shallow puddle. A single flat, arrowhead/triangle-shaped piece of clear ice floats in the puddle, its right half mirroring bright sky. To the left of the ice the water is darker and dotted with small bubbles and grit; pale stains and pebbles on the dry concrete form a fixed background.
visible_changes: The ice shard slowly rotates/drifts in place: comparing frame 1 to frame 41, the upper tip moves from roughly (505,35) down to about (540,120) while the right tip stays near (820-830,290-300) and the lower notch near (620-650,430), i.e. the piece pivots clockwise about its right end rather than translating across the scene.
The bright reflected highlight on the shard shifts shape and position as it turns, spreading from the right half toward the upper edge in later frames.
A thin strand of ice/water hangs from the bottom notch of the shard in the middle-to-late frames (around x=620-645, y=440-475), more pronounced than at the start.
Small ripples and bubbles on the left side of the puddle jitter and rearrange slightly over time.
Faint white sky-reflection patches appear in the open water to the left of the shard (near (410,320) and (440,420)) from about frame 13 onward.
The background concrete texture, stains and pebbles keep the same image positions throughout, indicating a static camera rather than camera motion.
outside_clip_unknowns: What initiated the shard's rotation and whether it continues, melts, or leaves the frame after the excerpt.
Whether the left-side water disturbances are from an unseen drip/current or natural settling.
uncertain_details: The exact cause of the slow rotation (current vs. settling) is not visible.
The white patches in the left water are consistent with sky/cloud reflections on a rippling surface but could also be small floating debris; not fully distinguishable.
Whether the shard also translates a little in addition to rotating is hard to separate from the rotation about its right tip.
